flags.title: SCPWA 3-Year SOL + Treble Damages — Strategic Wage Advantage
flags.summary: South Carolina Payment of Wages Act (SCPWA) provides a 3-year statute of limitations AND treble (3x) damages for wage theft. This is one of the strongest wage recovery provisions in the registry. File with SC DOL: 803-896-4300 / llr.sc.gov. Also dual-file federal WHD.

flags.title: Gullah Geechee Heirs Property — Unique Coastal Land Title Vulnerability
flags.summary: The Gullah Geechee corridor (Lowcountry coast from Charleston to Savannah) has widespread heirs property — land passed down without formal title. This makes families vulnerable to partition sales and tax foreclosure. SC Appleseed Legal Justice Center: 803-779-1113 / scjustice.org. Center for Heirs' Property Preservation: 843-745-7055 / heirsproperty.org.

flags.title: Catawba Indian Nation — Only Federally Recognized Tribe in SC
flags.summary: The Catawba Indian Nation near Rock Hill is the only federally recognized tribe in South Carolina. Catawba Nation: 803-366-4792 / catawba.com. For tribal members outside reservation: programs available with enrollment documentation.

flags.title: Upstate Latino Manufacturing Workforce — BMW/Michelin Corridor
flags.summary: The SC Upstate (Greenville-Spartanburg) has a growing Latino workforce in the BMW/Michelin manufacturing corridor. Language access and wage theft are common issues. SC Legal Services: 888-346-5592 / sclegal.org.

flags.title: UI 10-Day Appeal Deadline — Tied Second Shortest in Registry
flags.summary: South Carolina UI appeal deadline is 10 days from mailing — tied for second shortest in the registry. Contact legal aid within 5 days of any denial. SC DEW: 803-737-2400 / dew.sc.gov.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: South Carolina Emergency Admission
flags.message: SC involuntary psychiatric hold law: South Carolina Emergency Admission. Statutory authority: S.C. Code § 44-17-410. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in SC retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in SC: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: South Carolina Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: South Carolina Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
